segments.title: 第117章 揚名
segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Years Chapter 117: Making a Name

"This is just too outrageous..."

In the classroom of Class One.

Lin Xiuhong sat in Ying Chanxi's seat, holding the report card in her hand. Looking at the scores, each more outrageous than the last, she couldn't help but sigh in her heart.

With a report card like this in hand, she didn't even know how to lose.

Nine subjects, first in the school for seven of them. Among them, Math, Physics, and Chemistry were all full marks.

Out of a total of 1050 points, Ying Chanxi scored 1014. Across nine subjects, only 36 points were deducted in total.

This number of points, for the Li Luo from before, probably wouldn't even cover the deductions for one of his subjects.

Taking out Ying Chanxi's exam papers, every question was marked with a red check. There were few crosses, making it a pleasant sight to behold.

Even though Teacher Sun, who was conducting the parent-teacher conference, had a gloomy expression and reminded the parents of several students whose midterm grades had severely declined, Lin Xiuhong didn't have to worry about being called out by the teacher.

In fact, she even wished she would be called upon.

After all, as long as it was about Ying Chanxi, it would definitely be something good.

At most, he might worry about over-praising and add, "The topic of the Chinese composition was slightly misinterpreted this time, she needs to pay attention to that next time."

And that would be it. The rest would be all praise.

Lin Xiuhong curiously flipped through Ying Chanxi's composition.

The topic this time was about friendship during one's school days, a rather ordinary topic.

But Ying Chanxi only scored 42 out of 60 points on her composition. For other students, this might be considered average, but for Ying Chanxi, it was definitely an underperformance.

Of the 36 points deducted from her total score, half were from the composition.

"In this midterm exam, aside from student Ying Chanxi, whom I have praised countless times, there is another person I must commend."

Teacher Sun adjusted his glasses and looked at the slightly moved and expectant expressions of the parents below. He said with a deadpan face, "But unfortunately, the person I want to praise is not a student in our class, so it has nothing to do with any of you parents."

"But there is one thing I think everyone should realize."

"And that is, getting into an advanced class does not mean victory is assured."

"It's not that once you're in our Class One, admission to Qianjiang University is guaranteed. In previous years, many students from Class One have fallen behind during their three years of high school. We must be vigilant about this."

At this point, Teacher Sun paused his speech, then picked up a school-wide ranking list and said to the parents present, "Out of the top 40 in the entire school this time, our Class One only occupies 26 spots."

"Fourteen of our students were pushed out of the top 40, surpassed by students from the other advanced classes, Classes Two through Four."

"But that's not the main point."

"The main point is the student I'm about to mention, Li Luo, with a total score of 954, ranking 27th in the entire school."

At this, Teacher Sun paused again, glancing at the reactions of the parents below.

Many parents had a lukewarm reaction. After all, their own children scored higher than this Li Luo, so it didn't seem particularly surprising.

But in the next second, Teacher Sun added, "This student named Li Luo is not from an advanced class, but from a parallel class, Class Eight."

"At the same time, he is the only student from a parallel class to make it into the top 40 in the entire school for this midterm exam."

"Everyone, think carefully. Your children were all admitted through a selective autonomous enrollment process, yet in just a few short months, they've been surpassed by a student from a parallel class. We all need to seriously consider the reasons for this."

To be honest, many of the parents in Class One were already used to their children's excellence.

So, the parents whose children ranked in the top 30 of the school didn't feel a particularly deep impact.

But the parents whose children's scores were pushed out of the top 40 now wore solemn expressions, listening attentively to the head teacher's words.

However, at this very moment, among all the parents present, the person most shocked by what Teacher Sun said was, conversely, Lin Xiuhong, who was there for Ying Chanxi's parent-teacher conference.

Lin Xiuhong was completely stunned.

She thought something was wrong with her ears.

Or perhaps, this Li Luo that Teacher Sun mentioned just happened to have the same name as her son?

Lin Xiuhong's heart was filled with doubt, but as Ying Chanxi's parent, she felt it wasn't appropriate for her to ask directly.

Fortunately, Ying Chanxi, who was assisting Teacher Sun with the conference, had already approached him and curiously glanced at the list.

"Auntie Lin, it's true. Li Luo did really well this time."

To be honest, Ying Chanxi herself wasn't this happy even when she got first place.

But now, because Teacher Sun was publicly praising Li Luo, she couldn't stop the smile from spreading across her face.

"Really?" Lin Xiuhong was still a bit skeptical, finding it hard to believe that Li Luo could score so high and rank 27th in the whole school!

She recalled that when Li Luo ranked 86th in the high school entrance exam, Lin Xiuhong already felt like their ancestors' graves were emitting green smoke.

But now, including the 160 top students from the advanced classes who didn't take the high school entrance exam, Li Luo could still rank 27th.

This wasn't just ancestors' graves emitting green smoke, this was the ancestors' graves emitting a celestial green light.

"It's true," Ying Chanxi confirmed again. "There's only one Li Luo in Class Eight. Who else could it be?"

"Oh my... My heart is pounding." Lin Xiuhong's hands were trembling with excitement. "That kid, when did he become so capable..."

Lin Xiuhong had been worried before. After all, when Li Luo's uncle came for dinner, he had specifically warned them, suggesting that Li Luo temporarily stop writing web novels to avoid affecting his studies.

Lin Xiuhong did indeed share this concern.

But faced with Li Luo's monthly royalties of over 10,000 yuan and the promise he made to them, she still chose to believe him this one time.

Originally, Lin Xiuhong thought that as long as Li Luo could get into the top three hundred this time, that would be enough.

With three more years of hard work, and with Ying Chanxi helping to keep an eye on him, maybe he would have a shot at Qianjiang University.

But Lin Xiuhong never imagined that her son wouldn't just make it into the top three hundred.

He went straight into the top thirty!

Even the head teacher of the top advanced class, Class One, had to specifically mention and praise her son.

When Li Luo was in school before, Lin Xiuhong had never received such treatment at parent-teacher conferences.

This time, attending Xixi's parent-teacher conference, Lin Xiuhong had truly won big.

She got to experience the superiority of being the parent of the school's top student, and she also got to have her son praised by another class's head teacher.

It was truly a case of killing two birds with one stone.

"But it's still thanks to you tutoring him so well, Xixi. Otherwise, he wouldn't have been able to get such a high score." Lin Xiuhong happily held Ying Chanxi's hand and said softly, "With you always looking after him, I can rest much easier."

"Auntie Lin, you're being too kind. It's what I should do." Ying Chanxi smiled shyly. "And it's mainly because Li Luo himself worked hard. I just helped him review a little."

Meanwhile, in the classroom of Class Eight.

Although he couldn't savor the feeling of being the parent of the year's top student, Li Guohong's mood was no worse than Lin Xiuhong's.

Especially when Teacher Kong was speaking on the stage, he would mention Li Luo from time to time.

After all, Li Luo not only had good grades, placing first in the class, but he was also the class monitor of Class Eight, responsible for many things.

Basically, no matter what they talked about, it was impossible not to mention Li Luo, to the point that Li Guohong was floating on cloud nine from all the praise, barely able to contain the smile on his face.

Especially since Yan Zhusheng's mother, sitting next to him, would occasionally chat with him, asking for parenting advice and many questions about Li Luo.

Looking at the face that was so similar to his idol, Yuan Wanqing, and coupled with his euphoric state, Li Guohong let his guard down and shared everything about Li Luo from childhood to the present.

Thus, without any effort, Yuan Wanqing quickly got a detailed picture of the boy named Li Luo.

As the time neared ten in the morning and the final free Q&A and communication session of the parent-teacher conference ended, Kong Junxiang on the podium said:

"Next, our class's vice monitor and students from the student union will show you around the school."

"You'll get a feel for our learning atmosphere, club activities, and some of the school's basic facilities."

"Okay, you can go." Kong Junxiang smiled. "The other teachers and I will be at the gymnasium later. We look forward to your performance."

Li Luo nodded with a smile and then walked out of the classroom.

He happened to run into Ying Chanxi leading the parents of Class One downstairs for a tour, with Lin Xiuhong among them.

Ying Chanxi spotted Li Luo from around the corner and quickly said a word to the student next to her who was also responsible for leading the tour, then trotted over.

"You guys are quick," Li Luo said, glancing at Lin Xiuhong in the crowd. Seeing his mom's beaming face, it looked like she had received quite a bit of praise.

Ying Chanxi smiled sweetly and patted Li Luo's shoulder hard. "Not bad, you didn't disappoint me."

"You know already?" Li Luo raised an eyebrow. "I haven't even had the chance to show off yet."

"Oh, stop it. Our Teacher Sun already did all the showing off for you." Ying Chanxi rolled her eyes at him. "You have no idea how Teacher Sun praised you during the conference just now. Auntie Lin was overjoyed."

"Huh?" Li Luo was taken aback for a moment, then sighed, "I was waiting to show off to my mom again at lunchtime. Teacher Sun had to go and ruin all the fun."

"Aren't you childish?" Ying Chanxi said, exasperated, before adding with a grin, "Show a little of the magnanimity a 27th-ranked student in the school should have. Keep up the good work, and let's see if you can surpass me next time."

"You must be joking," Li Luo said, the corner of his mouth twitching.

He had already seen the school rankings at Kong Junxiang's desk. Ying Chanxi's total score was 1014. He had no idea how that girl managed to get a score like that.

Li Luo had given it his all in this exam, even with a powerful tool like the Memory Palace at his disposal.

And yet, he only ranked 27th in the school. This just went to show how ridiculous the people ahead of him were.

And Ying Chanxi, who had a full 16-point lead over the second-place student, was on a whole other level.

It felt like this was a gap that couldn't be closed by relying on the Memory Palace alone.

Talent, sometimes, was just truly unfair.

"Alright, I have to go lead the tour." Ying Chanxi patted Li Luo's shoulder. "You still have to go to the rock club, right? You'll be performing on stage soon."

"Yeah," Li Luo nodded. "I was just about to head over."

"Then you'd better go." Ying Chanxi turned and ran back towards the group of Class One parents. Halfway there, she turned her head back and waved at him. "Break a leg!"

(End of Chapter)
